subject: Corrective action playbook request and legal/HR review

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposal: corrective action playbook for A. Jenkins

Grace —

I pulled together an initial draft of a corrective action playbook for Alex Jenkins (attached) after our 1:1 earlier this week. Before I proceed with any formal notification, I need HR and Legal to confirm:

- Is the proposed 60-day timeline appropriate from an HR policy perspective, or should we compress/extend it?
- Are there any legal concerns with the documentation language (we call out monitoring of deliverables and access to project repos)?
- Any mandatory wording we need for accommodations or union/contracted staff triggers?

Attachment: corrective_playbook_draft.docx (outline + manager objectives + metrics)

High level: performance gaps are primarily around delivery consistency and peer feedback. I included measurable targets (weekly commit cadence, demo quality rubric) and a weekly 1:1 cadence. I want to be transparent with Alex, but avoid language that could be construed as punitive before HR/Legal review.

Can you both take a look and flag the items you want changed? If helpful, I can join a short alignment call — suggested times on my calendar: Tue 9/22 10:00-11:30 or Wed 9/23 2:00-4:00.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Product Engineering

Markus —

Thanks for sending this over. I reviewed the draft at a high level and pulled together a short packet of manager observations from the last two quarters (attached). I agree we should not notify Alex until HR and Legal sign off on the plan and the meeting script.

Quick notes after first pass:
- Remove any wording that implies intent to terminate (e.g., "probationary" phrasing) — Legal should suggest alternatives.
- Clarify success criteria to be measurable and achievable; some of the goals are currently time-based without clear acceptance criteria.
- Keep the initial notice conversational and supportive; include links to coaching resources and an offer for reasonable accommodations.

Attachment: manager_observations.pdf (notes + dates + examples)

I'll block 30 minutes on Wed 9/23 14:00 PT for a quick alignment unless you prefer Tue morning. Monica/Laura, can you confirm availability and whether you want me to draft the employee-facing notification text after you provide redlines?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
People Partner, EMEA & US

Date: 2026-09-22T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: corrective action playbook for A. Jenkins

Grace/Markus —

Thanks for the draft. I reviewed and attached the HR PIP template (PIP_template_v2.docx) which contains the minimum language we require for documentation, accommodation language, and a checklist for escalation triggers. Key HR asks:

- Timeline: standard is 45 days for individual contributor roles; we can extend to 60 days if there is a clear, documented reason (e.g., project ramp). Please outline why 60 days is preferred in the plan.
- Meetings: include an explicit weekly check-in and a mid-point formal review (written).
- Employee support: include coaching resources and a point person in People Ops.
- Documentation: keep records of all notes and manager feedback; HR must retain copies in the employee file.

Link to HR playbook: https://drive.redwood.com/HR/PIP_playbooks/drive-link-1234

One sensitive note — if there are confidentiality concerns around project repos or customer data, we need to get Legal involved (Laura), and possibly limit access during the PIP. Markus, can you confirm whether Alex's role includes any customer-facing privileges or access to regulated data? That will affect the phrasing.

I am available for the Wed 9/23 14:00 PT alignment. If you want HR to lead the initial notification meeting, say so and we will prepare the script. Otherwise, we recommend manager + HR in the room for the first conversation.

Attachment: PIP_template_v2.docx

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior People Partner
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: corrective action playbook for A. Jenkins — legal redlines

Team —

I reviewed the draft and HR template. Attached are tracked redlines (legal_redlines_corrective_playbook.docx). High-level legal guidance and recommended edits:

1) Tone & liability: Replace any language that could be interpreted as a waiver of employment rights or a contractual change. Use wording such as "This plan is intended to clarify performance expectations and provide support; it does not in itself alter employment status."
2) Data & access: If you intend to restrict repo or customer access, document the specific systems and rationale. Do not state monitoring methods in granular detail (we should avoid creating an impression of surveillance).
3) Confidentiality & third parties: Any involvement of external consultants (e.g., peopleops-consultant@workplaceconsults.com) requires written consent if the file contains personal data.
4) Timeline: HR's 45-day baseline is defensible; a 60-day plan is acceptable if justified. If you elect 60 days, add a clause for an interim 3-week checkpoint with documented outcomes.
5) Remedies & appeals: Add a short section describing next steps if objectives are not met and how the employee can raise concerns or request an appeal.

Please incorporate these edits and circulate the final manager + HR script. Once revised, email me the final package and I will provide formal sign-off or escalate if additional counsel review is needed.

Attachment: legal_redlines_corrective_playbook.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Legal
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: corrective action playbook for A. Jenkins

All —

Understood and thank you. I will update the draft to align with HR's 45-day baseline with an option to extend to 60 days, add the 3-week checkpoint, and remove the surveillance-style wording. I will send the revised package by end of day tomorrow and would appreciate legal sign-off after that.

I'll plan for manager + HR to run the initial meeting.

Regards,
Markus
